title: Rapid-Deployment Crack Measurement Based on SAM3 Semantic-Edge Response Decoding (SERD)
mechanism: SAM3's internal prompt-conditioned semantic response keeps crack evidence that its final masks suppress; calibrate it with a fixed Sobel field, training-free; also measures width/length directly.
adaptation: Use as a label-free crack prior map on E1-like half-cut cells and the 159k pool: extra input channel or soft teacher for the house model; width/length outputs feed severity.
min_experiment: Run SERD on val, F51 and H36; measure crack relR@2 at the house model's relP@2; kill if relR@2 < 0.4. Then house + SERD channel vs house PF on E1 crack recall.
evidence: R: 6 crack sets; internal response 82.66% crack-pixel recall vs 74.66% for SAM3 masks; width MAE 6.07 -> 5.55 px.

alt_notes.adaptation: Zero-shot crack-likelihood map for EL as an E1 diagnostic (house gives p < 0.001 to 70% of E1 crack pixels), as an extra input channel, and as a severity width estimator.
alt_notes.min_experiment: No training: SAM3 + SERD on val and F51; relR@2 / relP@2 for crack. Go if relR@2 >= 0.5 on F51; else close the SAM3 text-prompt route.
